text:
maya: heads up — noticed a big regression on console canary after the midday deploy. heatmap + multi-series charts stutter, main thread tasks spike to 400-600ms repeatedly :grimacing:
sam: ugh, saw alerts for LCP and CPU. is this the telemetry client change we shipped this morning? deploy-bot: deploy applied by ci/cd @ 11:12 UTC — telemetry-client@1.4.0, charting-lib@3.2.1
devon: can reproduce locally on latest canary. flame mostly in telemetry init + bundle parse. looks like telemetry eager-init moved a bunch of heavy io to main thread. stack snippet:
```
LongTask: parse main.js (120ms)
telemetry.init -> attachSampler -> syncParseFormats (80ms)
chart.render -> computeSeries -> layout(90ms)
```
li: interesting — telemetry sampler used to be async in 1.3.x. 1.4.0 added synchronous format parsing to dedupe schemas. i assumed it's small but looks not.
ande: can we gate the sampler behind worker thread? or fall back to a no-op on render-critical paths?
tess: timeline: console route does a prefix prefetch of telemetry helpers for chart pages, so they're landing on main before render. maybe prefetch policy changed too (prefetch priority increased) in the same rollout.
maya: yes — we changed prefetch priority to 'high' for telemetry helpers last week to reduce cold-start noise. combo is killing us.
sam: mitigation plan: 1) rollback telemetry-client to 1.3.x for canary, 2) revert prefetch priority on console routes, 3) quick patch to make telemetry.init async and off main thread. thoughts?
devon: rollback is fastest. will open a patch to 1.3.x pin and a rollback rollout.
li: i can prepare the async init patch but needs a small API change: expose initAsync() that schedules parsing in a worker and returns early. will PR in ~30m.
ande: for longer term, we should add a render-path quota: disallow sync telemetry parsing if route is 'dashboard' or if main-thread blocked over threshold. also add a canary flag to block prefetch for non-essential libs.
tess: agree on quota. also we need better telemetry for this: something that attributes main-thread stalls to specific packages so the console SLO page can alert on package-level regressions.
maya: created a perf playbook note: https://console.internal/perf/playbooks/series-thawing — contains reproducer steps, trace links, and rollback checklist.
sam: ok let's do rollback now. devon please start canary rollback, li start PR for async init, tess revert prefetch priority. i'll update the rollout ticket and page. :thumbsup:
devon: rolling back telemetry-client to 1.3.7 on canary now — patch in progress. will post status.
deploy-bot: rollback started by devops at 11:58 UTC — rolling to canary (2 pods)
maya: thanks everyone. after rollback, we should run a controlled perf test matrix: variations of prefetch priority + telemetry async vs sync to find safe defaults. add to next retro action items.
li: will also add a unit that detects heavy sync work in init and fails CI if >50ms on synthetic main-thread run.
ande: and we should add a routing policy doc snippet: critical render routes should be treated as low-priority for non-essential prefetches unless explicit opt-in. i'll draft.
maya: last: anyone spotted related quota/kv-cache issues? i saw some prefix cache misses but think they're secondary. if anyone sees spike in kvcache eviction, ping here.
sam: no kvcache spike in metrics, looks primary to telemetry parse. closing loop after rollback completes. :eyes:
